Delivered as a fake Adobe PDF Component AppX app bundle
Phishing emails impersonating company manager with threatening language
Malware harvests system information and sends it to command-and-control server disguised as cookies via HTTPS
Injection of malicious code into headless Chromium-based Edge browser process
Used to deliver additional payloads like Cobalt Strike beacons and Ryuk ransomware
Attack Vector: Highly targeted spam campaign with phishing emails
Phishing landing site hosted on Microsoft cloud storage (*.web.core.windows.net)
Use of ms-appinstaller: URL prefix to launch App Installer
Malicious files hosted on Microsoft cloud storage
User interaction to open App Installer and install malicious AppX bundle
Indicators of Compromise: Malicious .appinstaller and .appxbundle files hosted on Microsoft cloud storage
Phishing URLs with adobeview subdomain on *.web.core.windows.net domains
Payload named Security.exe nested within UpdateFix subfolder
Command-and-control server communication disguised as HTTPS cookies
SophosLabs Github page with IoCs including malware sample hashes, C2 server, and source URLs
